outcomes.text: Read a wide range of challenging classic literature and extended literary non-fiction such as essays, reviews and journalism, including whole texts.
Read at least one Shakespeare play.
Read works from the 19th, 20th and 21st centuries.
Read poetry since 1789, including representative Romantic poetry.
Re-read literature and other writing so as to make comparisons.
Choose and read books independently for challenge, interest and enjoyment.
Read in different ways for different purposes, summarising and synthesising ideas and information and judging how useful they are.
Use knowledge of a text's purpose, audience and social, historical and cultural context, and its literary tradition, to evaluate it.
Identify and interpret themes, ideas and information in a text.
Explore plot, characterisation, events and settings, how they relate and what effects they have.
Find evidence in the text to support a point of view and justify inferences with it.
Tell supported statements from unsupported ones, and spot bias and misuse of evidence.
Analyse a writer's choices of vocabulary, form, grammar and structure, and evaluate their effectiveness and impact.
Make critical comparisons of texts across context, themes, characterisation, style and quality, using wider reading.
Give an informed personal response, recognising that other responses are possible and weighing them.
Adapt writing to describe, narrate, explain, instruct, give and respond to information, and argue, for different purposes and audiences.
Select and organise ideas, facts and key points, and cite evidence, details and quotations effectively for support and emphasis.
Choose vocabulary, grammar, form, structure and rhetorical devices judiciously to suit audience, purpose and context, using Standard English where appropriate.
Make notes, draft and write, including using information supplied by others, such as writing a letter from given key points.
Reflect on whether a draft achieves its intended impact.
Restructure writing and amend grammar and vocabulary to improve coherence, consistency, clarity and effectiveness.
Check grammar, punctuation and spelling for accuracy and effectiveness.
Study the effectiveness and impact of grammar and vocabulary in texts read.
Take new vocabulary and grammatical constructions from reading and listening and use them deliberately for effect in writing and speech.
Analyse differences between spoken and written language, formal and informal registers, and Standard English and other varieties.
Use linguistic and literary terminology accurately and confidently when discussing reading, writing and speech.
Use Standard English in speech when context and audience require it.
Work in groups of various sizes, taking roles such as leading discussions, involving others, summarising and meeting deadlines.
Listen to and build on others' contributions, ask clarifying questions and challenge courteously.
Plan formal presentations and debates, selecting and organising information and ideas persuasively for the audience.
Listen and respond in formal and informal contexts, evaluating content, viewpoints, evidence and presentation.
Improvise, rehearse and perform scripts and poetry, using role, intonation, tone, volume, mood, silence, stillness and action for impact.
